name: First Residential District
allowed_uses: Single-family dwelling; school; church; community club house; nurseries, farms, truck gardens, greenhouses; usual accessories incl. home office of musician/physician/dentist and garage for not more than four automobiles; temporary construction buildings and a stable for not more than two cows or two horses by Board permit
max_units_per_lot: 1 (a two-family dwelling allowed if at least 5,000 sq ft of open area remains on the lot)
setbacks: none in zoning ordinance (front set-back lines were set street by street under separate ordinances)
notes: Ordinance No. 5464 (New Series), passed Oct. 3, 1921. A use-only ordinance: it regulated what a building was used for, not its size. The 5,000 sq ft open-area rule for two-family dwellings is in Sec. 3(7).
source: pipeline/data/raw/1921/20180102094111288.pdf (Sec. 1-3); passage date from pipeline/data/raw/1929/20180102100804566.pdf p.2

name: Second Residential District
allowed_uses: All First Residential uses plus tenement house or apartment house; flat; boarding or lodging house; hotel; library; public building; hospital or sanitarium; police station; fire station; philanthropic/eleemosynary institution (not correctional)
setbacks: none
notes: Apartments allowed as of right; no height, density or yard rules.
source: pipeline/data/raw/1921/20180102094111288.pdf (Sec. 4)

name: Commercial District
allowed_uses: Everything except a list of excluded trades: auto repair (unless part of a public garage), bakeries >5 employees, blacksmiths, bottling works, carting/storage yards, contractors' yards, cooperage, laundries >10 employees, lumber yards, uses excluded from Light Industrial, and manufacturing not incidental to retail (light manufacturing above the ground floor OK). Printing, newspapers, substations, phone exchanges allowed; public garages and gas stations by Board permit
max_units_per_lot: unlimited (all Sec. 3 and 4 residential uses expressly allowed)
setbacks: none
notes: Exclusion-based (cumulative) zoning: residential uses could not be excluded from Commercial. Per a 2017 history quoted by Collectors Weekly, a corner-store lot could host an apartment building or a skyscraper.
source: pipeline/data/raw/1921/20180102094111288.pdf (Sec. 5); pipeline/data/raw/1921/20180102094119011.pdf (Sec. 5 cont.)

name: Light Industrial District
allowed_uses: All Commercial uses plus most industry, except 27 listed noxious trades (acetylene/ammonia/asphalt/brick/celluloid/creosote/gas/gunpowder/lime/petroleum/potash manufacture, blast furnaces, boiler works, rolling mills, ship yards, smelting, stockyards, junk storage, acid manufacture, tar, wool pulling, yeast plants, nuisances by odor/dust/smoke/gas/noise) and Heavy-Industrial-only uses. Closed-furnace foundries by Board permit
max_units_per_lot: unlimited (single dwellings, flats and tenement houses allowed)
setbacks: none
notes: Housing was still permitted in Light Industrial.
source: pipeline/data/raw/1921/20180102094119011.pdf (Sec. 6)

name: Heavy Industrial District
allowed_uses: All uses except: single dwelling, flat or tenement house; abattoir; candle factory; distillation of coal/bones/wood; fat rendering; fertilizer, glue/size/gelatin manufacture; garbage incineration/reduction; tallow/grease/lard manufacture. Watchman's family quarters allowed
setbacks: none
notes: The only 1921 district that banned housing. The most noxious trades (abattoirs, rendering, etc.) were excluded even here; they went to Unrestricted.
source: pipeline/data/raw/1921/20180102094119011.pdf (Sec. 7)

name: Unrestricted District
allowed_uses: No use restrictions except those imposed by other law or ordinance
setbacks: none
source: pipeline/data/raw/1921/20180102094119011.pdf (Sec. 8)

name: District boundary rule
allowed_uses: Where two districts appear within one block, the boundary of the less restricted district is 100 ft back from its street line (blocks <=200 ft wide) or 137.5 ft / rear lot line (wider blocks)
notes: Explains the strips of Commercial zoning along streets on the 1921-1948 maps. The 1929 reprint adds that the line never extends more than 137.5 ft.
source: pipeline/data/raw/1921/20180102094127001.pdf (Sec. 15); pipeline/data/raw/1929/20180102100804566.pdf p.3
